intro: The indefinido tells a finished event. The imperfect tells a habit or the background of the scene.
p.ayer.consejo: It is a closed day, so it goes with the indefinido: «ayer compré». The initial y sounds as in «yo».
p.antes.consejo: With the imperfect it points to a habit: «antes viajaba en tren». It is the opposite of «ahora».
p.compré.consejo: The accent marks the last syllable: kom-PRÉ. Without it, «compre» is a different verb form.
p.compraba.consejo: -ar verbs form the imperfect with -aba. It talks about a habit: «compraba pan cada día».
p.llovió.consejo: «Llover» is only used in the third person. The ll sounds like y and the ó is the stressed syllable.
p.llovía.glosa: it was raining, it used to rain
p.llovía.consejo: It paints the rain as the background of the scene: «llovía cuando salí». The accent is on the í.
p.el billete.consejo: In Spain «billete» is used for train or plane. In many countries of America «boleto» or «pasaje» is used.
p.todo el día.consejo: It is a fixed time expression: «todo el día». With «ayer» it describes a whole episode.
p.en tren.consejo: With vehicles you say «en»: en tren, en bus, en avión. But «a pie» and «a caballo» take «a».
p.viajaba.consejo: Viajar is written with v and j, like «viaje». The j sounds like a soft h.
p.salí.consejo: A single event: «salí de casa a las ocho». The accent marks the last syllable: sa-LÍ.
b1.texto:
The choice depends on how you tell the past.

- **Indefinido**: a **finished event**, an episode with a beginning and an end.
- **Imperfecto**: a **habit**, an action **in progress**, or the **background** of the scene.

Look:

- Ayer **compré** un billete. (one purchase, finished)
- Antes **viajaba** en tren. (a habit)
- **Llovía** cuando **salí** de casa. (the rain is the background; **salí** is the event)
- Ayer **llovió** todo el día. (the rain is a complete episode inside a closed day)

A finished event can happen once or several times: what matters is that you tell it **as closed**.
b2.f0.texto: How did you travel back then?
b2.f1.texto: I used to travel by train.
b2.f2.texto: And how did you travel yesterday?
b2.f3.texto: Yesterday I bought a bus ticket.
b2.f4.texto: Was it raining when you left home?
b2.f5.texto: It was raining when I left home.
b2.f6.texto: Yesterday it rained all day here.
b2.f7.texto: Back then I used to buy the ticket at the station.
b4.texto:
Compare the two forms with the same verb:

- **comprar**: **compré** (closed event) / **compraba** (habit)
- **llover**: **llovió** (complete episode) / **llovía** (background)
- **viajar**: **viajé** (one trip) / **viajaba** (habitual trips)

Words that help:

- Usually with the **indefinido**: **ayer, anoche, el lunes pasado, de repente**.
- Usually with the **imperfect**: **antes, siempre, cada día, de niño**.

When one action **interrupts** another, the one in progress goes in the imperfect and the interrupting one in the indefinido: **Llovía cuando salí.**
b4.e1.texto: We used to buy the tickets at the station.
b4.e2.texto: It was raining a lot when I got home.
b5.f0.texto: I used to travel every summer on a slow, blue train.
b5.f1.texto: The windows trembled with every bend of the road.
b5.f2.texto: The fields passed slowly on the other side of the glass.
b5.f3.texto: My mother carried bread and cheese in a cloth bag.
b5.f4.texto: I watched the mountains until the last minute.
b5.f5.texto: Yesterday I bought a ticket for the afternoon train.
b5.f6.texto: Yesterday it rained all day on the grey city.
b5.f7.texto: I left home with a small suitcase.
b5.f8.texto: When I reached the platform, the air smelled of wet iron.
b5.f9.texto: At last, the train appeared through the mist with a long whistle.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: «antes» and the imperfect mark a habit.
b6.o1.refuerzo: It is one specific, finished purchase.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It tells a complete episode of a closed day.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence tells a past habit?
b7.o0.refuerzo: It would present the rain as a closed event, not as background.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Well done! The rain was in progress when «salí» happened.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is present: the sentence is about the past.
b7.pregunta: Which form paints the rain as background?
b8.traduccion: Back then I travelled a lot by train
b9.o0.refuerzo: It would be a habit, and «ayer» points to a specific day.
b9.o1.refuerzo: It is present, and the sentence is about yesterday.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That's it! A closed event on a closed day: indefinido.
b9.pregunta: Which form tells a finished purchase?
b10.o0.refuerzo: It points to a closed day: it asks for the indefinido.
b10.o2.refuerzo: It is a specific, finished moment.
b10.pregunta: Which word usually goes with a habit?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Well done: dinner was in progress when the call came.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It presents dinner as a complete event, not as the background of the call.
b12.o2.refuerzo: It is present, and the call already happened.
b12.pregunta: Which form shows dinner in progress?
p.viajabas.consejo: The -abas ending is the imperfect for tú.
p.viajaste.consejo: The -aste ending is the past for tú: «viajaste» is one finished trip.
p.comprábamos.consejo: The accent shows the stress on -prá-, in the middle.
p.billetes.consejo: «Billete» is a ticket. The double l sounds like y.
p.temblaban.consejo: The -aban ending marks an ongoing past action.
p.curva.consejo: Since it ends in -a, it is feminine: «la curva».
p.pasaban.consejo: The s is soft here: pa-SA-ban.
p.llevaba.consejo: The ll sounds like y: ye-BA-ba.
p.apareció.consejo: The accent is on the last syllable: a-pa-re-THYÓ.
p.silbido.consejo: It ends in -o, so it is masculine: «el silbido».
p.llamaste.consejo: The -aste ending is the past for tú.
p.cenaba.consejo: The c before e sounds like th: the-NA-ba.
